title: River Review Flow definition
description: Runtime-independent definition of WHEN and HOW review judgment is executed (#2013, Epic #2011). Skill = what to judge, Agent = who is responsible, Flow = when/how judgment is executed. A Flow document declares an ordered step list only; it never declares judgment criteria. Per ADR-009 D3/D4 the criteria (which skill is selected, severity vocabulary, gate/completion meaning) stay in `skills/**`, `docs/review/**`, `pages/reference/**` and `src/lib/**`, so every step object here is closed and carries no parameter bag. Unknown vocabulary is rejected at load time: every enum is closed and every object sets `additionalProperties: false`, so an unknown `use:` primitive, an unknown `agent:` role, or an unknown stop condition fails validation instead of being silently skipped. That matches the repository-wide fail-safe direction recorded in `src/lib/gate-decision.mjs` ("everything unknown or undetermined maps to NO_GO").

id.description: Flow identifier. Unique within the repository, stable across versions.

version.description: Semantic version of this Flow as a versioned asset, following the `packs:`/`skills:` convention (`schemas/pack.schema.json`). This is an asset version, not an artifact `schemaVersion`. The same `id` + `version` MUST mean the same execution semantics on every runtime (Claude Code, Codex, CLI). Breaking changes follow the policy in `pages/reference/stable-interfaces.md`.

intent.description: Why this Flow exists. Declarative label only; it does not select skills.

inputs.description: Named inputs the Flow may branch on. A step's `when` clause may only reference a name declared here, which keeps conditional execution free of an expression language.

steps.description: Ordered execution units. Array order IS the execution order: a conforming runtime MUST execute the steps in index order, so two runtimes given the same document produce the same ordering. Steps marked `parallel: true` may run concurrently with the adjacent `parallel: true` steps that form one contiguous run, but the run occupies the position of its first member and its results are collected in index order, so the observable ordering stays deterministic.

outputs.description: Artifacts this Flow is responsible for producing.

stopConditions.description: Conditions that stop the Flow. Values reuse the existing gate reason vocabulary (`GATE_REASON_CODES` in `src/lib/gate-decision.mjs`) rather than introducing a second reason-code system; `tests/flow-schema.test.mjs` pins the two lists together. The #2013 sketch values map onto it as `missing-required-artifact` -> `DETERMINISTIC_UNRUNNABLE` and `human-judgment-required` -> `HUMAN_APPROVAL_REQUIRED`.

stepPrimitive.description: The Flow step vocabulary. Single source of truth for the primitive names; every other document referring to a primitive MUST use one of these spellings. Each primitive names an existing capability rather than new behaviour (for example `select-skills` -> `selectSkills` in `runners/core/review-runner.mjs`, `derive-gate` -> `deriveGateDecision` in `src/lib/gate-decision.mjs`).

reviewerRole.description: Reviewer role id. Values are exactly the keys of `REVIEWER_ROLES` in `src/lib/reviewer-orchestrator.mjs`; `tests/flow-schema.test.mjs` pins the two lists together so a Flow cannot invent a third role ledger.

required.description: When true and the input is absent, the Flow stops. Absent means false.

when.description: Conditional execution, deliberately limited to presence of a declared input. There is no expression language: a Flow may not encode judgment criteria (ADR-009 D3).

onUnsatisfied.description: What a runtime does when a step cannot run as declared (its input is missing, its underlying capability is unavailable, or it fails). The three outcomes are distinct: `stop` halts the Flow and derives a gate carrying a `stopConditions` reason; `skip` does not execute the step, records a reason (the `{step, reasons[]}` shape already used by `evaluateSkill`) and continues; `degrade` executes a reduced form, records the degradation (the `plannerFallback` / partial-failure shape already used by `runners/core/review-runner.mjs` and `src/lib/reviewer-orchestrator.mjs`) and continues. Omitting the key means `stop`: the default is the safe side, so a Flow can only opt into continuing.

step.description: Exactly one of `use` (a Flow primitive) or `agent` (a reviewer role). Both objects are closed and carry no parameter bag, so selection criteria cannot be embedded in a Flow.

parallel.description: Marks this step as a member of the contiguous parallel run it belongs to. Absent means false (sequential).
